name: Product tips and updates
description: Announces two or three things worth turning on, each with what it does, who gets it, and the one action that enables it.

origin.note: Design: feature briefing — split opening, per-feature rows with availability chips and paired actions.

subject: {{ headline }}
preheader: Three things you can switch on today, none of which need a developer.

credits.author: Olly
credits.title: Cheerful diverse colleagues working on a laptop during a startup project

credits.author: Silverkblack
credits.title: Office workers discussing at a table with a laptop and colour swatches

credits.author: Jack Sparrow
credits.title: Man having an online meeting in an office

eyebrow.description: Small label above the headline, naming the release or the month.

headline.description: What the whole email is about, in one claim. Also the subject line by default.
headline.example: Three upgrades you can ship without a developer

intro.description: One paragraph setting up the list. Say what they have in common.
intro.default: Each of these is a switch in your settings rather than a project. None of them need a release.
intro.example: Each of these is a switch, not a project.

hero_image.description: Image for the opening split. A screenshot of the product beats a photograph of people; use a photograph only if you have nothing real to show.

features.description: One entry per thing being announced: `image`, `chip` (who gets it), `title`, `text`, `action_label`, `action_url`, and optional `learn_label` / `learn_url` for the secondary action.

closing_text.description: Closing paragraph, restating what is included.

reply_note.description: The reply invitation. Sending from a monitored address and saying so measurably raises replies.
reply_note.default: Questions? Reply to this email and it reaches the team that built these.

unsubscribe_note.description: How to stop these without leaving the product. Required in spirit on anything classed as marketing.
unsubscribe_note.default: You're getting this because you have an account. You can stop product updates and keep your account email.
